title: Better International ETF: Schwab's SCHF vs. the iShares IEFA
author: Robert Izquierdo
description: The article compares two international equity ETFs targeting developed markets outside the U.S. SCHF offers a lower expense ratio (0.03% vs 0.07%) and stronger 1-year performance (29.3% vs 21.8%), with significant exposure to South Korean semiconductor companies. IEFA provides greater scale ($196B AUM), broader diversification (2,616 holdings), and higher dividend yield (3.3% vs 3.0%). The choice depends on investor priorities: SCHF for AI/semiconductor exposure and lower costs, IEFA for liquidity and small-cap international exposure.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: SCHF demonstrates superior 1-year performance (29.3%), lower expense ratio (0.03%), and strategic exposure to high-growth South Korean semiconductor companies (Samsung, SK Hynix) benefiting from AI trends. Lower share price post-2024 split also improves accessibility.

IEFA offers significant advantages including massive scale ($196B AUM), superior liquidity, broader diversification (2,616 holdings), higher dividend yield (3.3%), and exposure to international small-cap stocks. Better for risk-averse investors seeking comprehensive developed market exposure.
Significant holding in both funds (2.58% in IEFA, 2.21% in SCHF), indicating strong positioning in semiconductor equipment manufacturing, a key beneficiary of AI infrastructure growth.

title: ASML Bets Big on AI & Capacity Expansion: Should You Buy the Stock?
author: Na
description: ASML is well-positioned to capitalize on AI-driven demand for advanced semiconductors, with plans to ship approximately 65 Low-NA EUV systems in 2026 and expand capacity by 30% in 2027. However, growth remains dependent on sustained customer spending and faces headwinds from export restrictions, geopolitical tensions, and potential cyclical downturns in semiconductor capital spending.

The neutral sentiment balances bullish fundamentals against material downside risks.

title: Why ASML Holding Stock Bumped 4% Higher Today
author: Eric Volkman
description: ASML Holding stock rose 4% following a bullish analyst report from Lynx Equity Strategies on memory chipmakers Micron Technology and Sandisk. The report cited strong prospects for these chipmakers as they ramp up production to meet AI-driven demand for computing power. ASML, which supplies essential lithography systems to chipmakers, is positioned to benefit from this industry expansion.
